checks.rule: fall confirmation creates ho-evt-001 and task-evt-001-01 (origin product_rule, anchor fixed, due_at = that day 20:00, assignee from the rota) and one needs_clinical_confirmation citing evt-001 r1; case_version +1, seq +1
after the fall confirmation every clinician-sourced item and instruction keeps its unchanged hash (every field of the latest version except cites, with the schedule reduced to its approved basis)
impact_set of the new clinician source == {task-B-01, ho-B-upcoming, ed-B-appointment} (items citing the superseded segment)

every new version satisfies must_contain / must_not_contain and is pending_review; a rewritten or delivered replacement text may not restate a superseded time, add a time, number or weekday (a number written as a word counts: 'two' == '2'), drop one the item stated that its sources still state, or relax an instruction (R17a-c, R17g-i, R17k); an item left for a person's rewrite is judged against the instruction it waits for (its current time and cited sentence), so it cannot restate the old time but can be rewritten with the facts of its current source, dropping what the change removed (an old condition, an earlier time), and the new version cites that source, also after a transcript correction (R17d-f, R17j-n); a later readable time of that instruction reaches the items left for a person and regenerates them (R4c); an item whose text already states the new time keeps its text and cites the new source (R4d, R4f); after an earlier time nobody could read, an item whose text states none of the instruction's readable times goes to a person (R4e); a transcript correction never regenerates an item that waits for a person's rewrite (a time or a condition), so approve-all cannot approve it, and the person's rewrite cites the instruction's current source (R23); a time-only recording never discharges a wait for a condition a change introduced, nor after a rejected rewrite brought the old text back, and a rewrite stating the condition is accepted (R27); after a restore two changes back the rewrite states and cites the current time and source (R30); a clock correction written the transcript's way ('4 p.m.' -> '5 p.m.', or with its weekday) moves the instruction time, the schedule and the items, and a rewrite restating the corrected-away clock is refused (R33); the corrected time is read from the corrected clause that stated it, never from the first weekday and clock of the whole sentence: a wording correction elsewhere in the sentence leaves the time, a correction of part of the clause ('at 4' -> 'at 5') or of the clause in a sentence that names another weekday first moves it, and a clause corrected to words without a readable clock ('Thursday morning', '4.30 p.m.', 'half past four') is an unreadable time with a needs_transcript_check question, its items rewritable with those words and exportable; a later correction to '4:30 p.m.' makes it readable (R38, R44); a clock matches only its own half of the day: a move or a correction from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. (or 11 a.m. to 11 p.m., 4 p.m. to 4 a.m.) regenerates the items and exports, and a text at the other half of the day is refused, delivered or approved (R39, R40); when one new sentence grounds two instruction changes, the rewrites cite only that sentence, never a superseded one, and a later correction of the superseded sentence leaves them approved (R45)

before review task-B-01/task-B-02 keep due_at Thu 11:00 and assignee cg-incoming while proposed_* show Wed 16:00 cg-outgoing; after approval due_at moves and the review event carries schedule_diff[basis=approved]; a second change before any review still leaves the approved basis at Thu 11:00 (R13a)

ins-B-001 keeps its id, time Wednesday 4:00 p.m., cites src-C-001-tx r1, derivation_status pending_review, previous.time Thursday 11:00 a.m., supersedes_overlap >= 0.5; a condition changes only when the cited verified sentence states it and it does not read as a relaxation, and the change is listed as condition_from/condition_to; a condition that differs only in case, whitespace or outer punctuation is no change (R12); previous is the last approved state while changes stack up unreviewed, and a rejection restores that state (R13); a superseding proposal whose action states another number (dose, count) or negation, the weekday and clock of either time set aside, is a pending change of the action (action_from/action_to, previous.action, a needs_clinical_confirmation question, every item resting on it left for a person's rewrite at the new dose, which then exports one dose only; a rejection restores the old action and its approved text), never applied under the old action or recorded as a confirmation, and one that rewords the action without changing the time, the condition or a number is refused (ValueError) (R26); an action that names the new weekday is a move, and one that names the same time a confirmation (R46); rejecting an instruction nobody ever approved withdraws it, also after a transcript correction or a later recording changed it, with its task (R29); a transcript correction of a dose the action states changes the action (a question is opened, its items follow, rejecting that change is refused, a counter-correction brings it back) (R41); a rejection restores the condition of the approved state, never the one the rejected change brought, also after a wording or a time correction (R42); a transcript correction of a condition's words changes the condition, its items follow, the corrected-away word is refused and rejecting that change is refused (R43)
task-C-01 exists, due with task-B-01: its proposed_due_at equals task-B-01's
every id in expected.unchanged keeps its unchanged hash; nothing outside allowed_schedule_follow changes its proposed schedule; untouched_hashes on the event equal the hashes after the event
case_version +1 exactly once, seq +1; old versions are superseded with superseded_by

same request_id + same payload -> replayed true, same change_id, no new version / pending / seq; same request_id + different payload -> ConflictError (409); same content_sha256 under another source_id -> replayed (matched_by content_sha256); the same recording with different proposals -> ConflictError, never a silent replay (R19)
an older recording: impact_set [], superseded_on_arrival_by on both source records, status recorded_no_change, case_version unchanged, both timestamps kept

a family statement opens exactly one conflict with about_instruction (the active instruction it shares the most words with; with none in common, the first timed one: R11b) and changes nothing else; a later clinical source confirming that instruction's time marks the conflict resolved_by and changes nothing else (recorded_no_change, reaffirmed_same_time)

task-evt-001-01 latest version has schedule.status cancelled and is pending_review; the question opened by the confirmation is closed with closed_reason; an event re-judged as a fall creates (or re-confirms) the note, the process task and the question like a first confirmation, and the notice says so, and approve-all approves the note and task it creates (R16); the engine's template task of a new timed instruction whose action names its weekday states the whole time, so approve-all approves it (R48)
after the re-judge every clinician-sourced item and instruction keeps its unchanged hash
a superseding proposal without a time keeps ins-B-001.time, marks nothing stale, records instruction_changes reaffirmed_no_time and opens one needs_clinical_confirmation

a job whose base_case_version is stale is refused (stale_generation), its content is kept only as discarded_content and never published; a job with a current base publishes through apply_change (change_event, case_version +1); a job started before a review withdrew its item (or the instruction it rests on) is refused as stale, and no job starts on an item of a withdrawn instruction (R28); an archived export is never regenerated: start_generation refuses an exported_pdf id (ConflictError) (R32)

export_pdf raises PendingReview with the pending ids while anything is stale or pending_review; after approval pdf-v5.case_version == case_version, seq matches, schedule rows show Wed 16:00, no 'Thursday'; pdf-v2 is byte-equal; a pdf_id that exists (an item, an instruction, an earlier export) or does not start with 'pdf-' is refused (guards); a rejection restores only versions a person approved and withdraws what the rejected change produced, so nothing contradicting the restored instruction can be approved or exported (R14, R15); a restored version comes back approved only if it passes the checks a delivered text passes against the case as it is now (the instruction time, the source revision, the corrections), else stale for a person, so approve-all cannot approve it and the export stays blocked (R14c, R14d, R15b, R15c); rejecting the instruction afterwards brings the approved text back (R14e); rejecting an instruction change that came from a transcript correction puts the instruction back on the earlier revision and leaves its item stale, the person's rewrite cites the corrected revision, and approve-all and the export then succeed (R14f-h); rejecting an instruction change also sends back every version made for it, a delivery or a person's rewrite (pending or approved on its own) that no longer fits, to its approved text when that fits, also after a condition change or an unreadable time (R24, R34); a restore is judged against every instruction the item rests on (a regenerated item keeps them all in derived_from), so a restore missing a new condition comes back stale and the export stays blocked until the rewrite (R25); items stale for a rejected instruction get their approved text back when it fits, and no rewrite cites the rejected change's sentence (R31); a reject never leaves an instruction at a time a transcript correction removed: rejecting the change a time correction made is refused (a counter-correction is the way back), and rejecting a later change keeps the correction (pending review, items rewritable at the corrected time) (R35); nothing that no longer fits the case is approved or exported: named ids are refused (NotFit), approve-all approves the rest and lists it in reviewed.refused, and an approved item that no longer fits blocks the export (ExportBlocked) until a person's rewrite (R36); found by a random walk over the engine (every reachable state can still be exported after a person's rewrites, and no export contradicts the approved instructions): a transcript correction never brings back a withdrawn item or instruction, a time nobody could read never forbids the same time in a rewrite, every rejected time stays forbidden (not only the last one), an item approved on its own for a never-approved instruction is withdrawn with it, and an item that still cites a rejected sentence is rewritten from the instruction's current one (R37); rejecting one of two instruction changes grounded in one sentence leaves the other instruction's approved item approved and brings the rejected instruction's approved text back, while an item of the other instruction that states the rejected time goes back (R47)
changes_for(cg-incoming): events and recorded_only counts equal the JSON; the banner is the exact string; every card carries the affected items' live review_status
after mark_seen unread is false; after another change it is true again; mark_seen refuses a seq or case_version ahead of the log, a bool, a negative or a non-integer (guards)
atomicity: an exception injected into any handler leaves snapshot_hashes, case_version, seq and requests unchanged
scoping: a second store (scenario_normal) keeps its snapshot_hashes after every Case C step; a source_id or instruction of another case raises NotInCase (404)

roles and input shape: a caregiver approving -> PermissionError (403); a family_statement carrying instructions -> ValueError (400); a clinical upload with source_type family_statement -> ValueError (400); recorded_at is a naive ISO local time, compared as a datetime (R20, guards); a transcript segment needs its own verified_by tick (R21); event ids are short tokens, the score a number, the actor a short label, an utterance at most 500 characters (R22, guards); a source revision is 'rN' (guards); none of them may end in a newline (guards); a proposal's quote is matched like any text (case, curly quotes, whitespace runs and line breaks do not refuse it) and a quote of punctuation only is refused (R21b, R21c)

confirmation roles: a clinician (role care_team) approves clinical content; the case's one primary family caregiver may confirm a pending version on the clinician's behalf only when it has waited longer than the case's time limit (on_behalf_after_hours, default 24, a case setting a clinician changes) (counted from the change's effective_at: never earlier than the latest 'at' already accepted, never the upload's uploaded_at) or the primary caregiver marked the clinician unreachable with a reason at or after the change became pending; the exclusion rule fails closed: an instruction only when its action, now and approved, is one of two non-medication templates (attend an appointment; bring a document or an aid) with a condition of appointment words only, and the change is a new such instruction or a time-only move; an item version only when every instruction it rests on is allowed, its numbers (in order, digits glued to units and number words included), negating and stop words are unchanged, no changed sentence names a medication or a verb that gives one, no letter is outside plain ASCII and every added word is grounded in its approved text or its instructions; so never a medication or dose change (a new medication, a changed number, a stop or a negation) nor a changed condition; and only a version that fits the case (the approve gate); named ids are refused as a whole (PermissionError or NotFit, nothing changes), confirm-all confirms the rest and lists the others with their reasons; a confirmed version is approved (in force) and labelled 'confirmed by the primary caregiver on the clinician's behalf' with its trigger in the item's state, the change log, the handover view (a card and the banner) and the exported PDF; a clinician later confirms it (clinician-confirmed) or rejects it on the normal path (the last approved state comes back, still labelled when it was itself confirmed on the clinician's behalf; a further rejection reaches the clinician's own approved state, never withdrawing it and never looping); while a newer change is pending the on-behalf version in force keeps its label in the handover view (in_force_confirmation, the banner, confirmations with basis in_force_while_change_pending); the time of a withdrawn instruction never stays in an approved text that cites its sentence; a clinician's action clears the unreachable mark; the primary caregiver, the time limit and the mark are validated (one caregiver label, whole hours, a one-line reason of at most 200 characters, plain ASCII letters, that never reads as a relaxation and names no medication, dose, number or stop; every change's 'at' a naive local minute); a non-primary caregiver, a clinician or a caregiver changing the settings is refused (PermissionError)
